atoms.text: Bonnie wants to show you around the cities in Scotland. Will you visit some cities with her?

instruction.text: Bonnie wants to know if you recognise what Scottish towns and cities look like. Select the three images of towns and cities in Scotland.

feedback.end: A lot of Scottish towns and cities are built near the coast. Nearly half of Scotland’s population live by the sea!
feedback.wrong: This is a town in South America. Scottish houses are usually less colourful and built from bricks.

instruction.text: Bonnie asks if you know what you might find in Scottish towns and cities. Drag the images to the correct words.

hint.text: An abbey is a type of religious building used by monks and nuns.
hint.label: Abbey

instruction.text: Bonnie has marked a few of Scotland’s biggest cities on her map. Find Glasgow on the map to visit it.
This is Glasgow. Find the bridge in the image to learn more.

feedback.end: Glasgow is not Scotland’s capital city, but it is the biggest and most populated city in the country.

instruction.text: Find Aberdeen on the map to visit it.
This is Aberdeen. Find the statue in the image to learn more.

feedback.end: Aberdeen is the third most populated city in Scotland. It has strong links to the North Sea through fishing, shipping and oil.

instruction.text: Find Inverness on the map to visit it.
This is Inverness. Find the houses in the image to learn more.

feedback.end: Inverness is known as the capital of the Scottish Highlands. It is the only city in this area. A quarter of all people in the Highlands live here.
